solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Indication of virtue by low-down element

parts.note: a saint is shown with a halo to signal goodness
the low-down is the inside information, British slang gen

explanation.surface: Some low-down element passes itself off with a show of virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, the same thing as the low-down. 'Low-down element' reads as a sneaky person, but the element is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine form the halogen group of chemical elements.

clue.text: Chemist offering heroin, a case of it

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
taken as written

indicators.note: a case is the outer covering, so only the outside letters of a word are kept

parts.note: 'it' points back to heroin, whose first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A dodgy chemist offers heroin, and a whole case of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemist is Otto Hahn, the German who discovered nuclear fission. 'It' is heroin again, and its case is the outer pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Hahn won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering nuclear fission, a famous named scientist.

clue.text: Back in jail, prisoner no longer accepting one's set of terms

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so just that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of jail

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a former prisoner is an ex-con
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former inmate, back in jail, picks up the jargon of the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in jail' looks like a prisoner returning, but it only yields the final letter of jail. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is the vocabulary of a language or subject, a collection of its words.

clue.text: Kid endlessly on his Nintendo?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a boy on his Nintendo console is playing video games

explanation.surface: A child plays on his games console without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it describes the child's playing time, but it cuts the last letter. Nintendo is a Japanese video-game maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a neglected young child running wild in a city.

clue.text: Flier's eccentric garment with skin of cheetah

parts.note: an eccentric person is a nut
a hat is an item of clothing

indicators.note: skin is the outer layer, so only the outside letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of cheetah

explanation.surface: A pilot sports an odd outfit trimmed with cheetah fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small climbing songbird, and any bird can be called a flier.

clue.text: Researcher's not genuine, back on the job

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: going back means running the letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: cod means fake or mock, as in a cod accent

explanation.surface: A scientist turns out to be a fraud, yet is back at work.
explanation.walkthrough: COD is British informal for sham or mock. 'On' places the reversed piece after the other, as in a down-style build of the across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is a researcher holding a post after completing a doctorate, usually in a university laboratory.

clue.text: Dog turning up, sure to be barking

indicators.note: turning something round sends its letters the other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hound shows up, certain to start yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' and 'barking' paint a noisy animal, but dog is a verb here and barking means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, trailing or hounding them.

clue.text: Queen's in bed, somewhat likely to feel sick

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a seam is a bed or layer of coal or rock
QU is an abbreviation for queen
ish means somewhat, to some degree

explanation.surface: The monarch has taken to her bed, feeling rather queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a bedroom, but it is a geological layer. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is easily nauseated or upset by unpleasant sights.

clue.text: Favourite line put in bold

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another

parts.note: bold means daring
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A cherished sentence is set in bold type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold' suggests typography, but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a favourite, someone treated as specially loved, as in the darling of the critics.

clue.text: Firms head without assurance for fair competition

parts.note: CO is company, and two of them are firms
nut is slang for head
lacking confidence is being shy

explanation.surface: Businesses whose boss lacks confidence want a level playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair competition' reads as fair play, but the fair is a funfair. A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where balls are thrown to knock coconuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a game played at a travelling funfair, where contestants try to win prizes by throwing balls.

clue.text: Test comprehended by unusual three or six-footer

indicators.note: to be comprehended by is to be taken in, held within
unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A puzzling exam question: is it a three-footer or a six-footer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is a line of verse with six metrical feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexameter is a line of poetry containing six metrical feet, as in Homer's epics.

clue.text: Such languages one caught by Hungary regularly

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'such' makes the phrase describe a kind of language

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Such tongues are picked up in Hungary as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, so the other pieces follow. Hungarian is itself one of the Ugric languages, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ugric branch of the Finno-Ugric family includes Hungarian and two Siberian tongues.

clue.text: Do lie in chat

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle, or con, them
fabulation is the telling of invented stories

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip a fib into conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like an instruction or a party, but it is a verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A confabulation is an informal conversation, the full form of the word confab.

clue.text: Blocks view of churchgoers hidden by screens

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing sits inside or behind it

parts.note: blinds are window screens
a congregation is the fold, the flock of the faithful

explanation.surface: Screens block the view of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: it takes an object, as the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To blindfold someone is to cover their eyes so that they cannot see anything.

clue.text: The French knight admitted to relative indulgence

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: to be admitted to a place is to be let inside it

parts.note: a niece is a relative
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A French knight is let in to see a relative indulging him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative indulgence' reads as a comparative amount of pampering; relative is a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniency and indulgence both mean treating someone mildly, without the strictness they might deserve.

clue.text: Shocks in the Spanish exam in kind of US college

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, the kind of college rather than the college itself

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, shock treatment
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A Spanish student gets a shock in an oral exam at an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electoral College is the body of electors that formally chooses the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electoral College is the group whose votes elect the American president, so electoral names the sort.

clue.text: Improvise in gin rummy, cutting card

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag, a wit

indicators.note: rummy is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters come out peculiar

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In a game of gin rummy you make it up as you go, cutting the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin rummy' is the card game, but rummy signals the shuffle and card is a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: To wing it is an idiom for doing something without preparation, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: Got rid of current measure for gas

parts.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: An old gas meter has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current measure' reads as a present-day policy, but it is the unit of electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane found in coal mines, an explosive gas feared by miners.

clue.text: Swan around with man and wife's kinsman

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so letters run backwards

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a man is a he
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A relative wanders about with a married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan around' reads as idle wandering, but swan is a noun whose female is a pen. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a male relative, the son of a sibling, so a kinsman.

clue.text: Model's head in painting by surrealist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of painting
Louis Aragon was a French surrealist poet

explanation.surface: An artist's model has her head in a surrealist painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' sounds like a sitter for an artist, but it means a perfect example. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example to be imitated.

clue.text: Speaking drunkenly, neglect religious ceremony in confusion

indicators.note: a drunk slurs sibilants, so the words are said with a slushy sound

parts.note: to skip church is to miss Mass; a slurred voice turns each S sound to SH

explanation.surface: A drunkard slurs that he has skipped the service and is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The drunk tries to say miss Mass and it comes out mishmash, a slurred S becoming SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, a muddled mixture of disparate things.

clue.text: Means of transport, or pretentiousness with it

parts.note: putting on airs is being pretentious
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Choosing how to travel: something practical, or showing off in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like a joining phrase, but it means trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a lighter-than-air craft such as a zeppelin, a vehicle that carries passengers.

clue.text: Balance is wrong on TV

parts.note: off means wrong, as in off the mark
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A complaint that the colour balance on the television is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balance' looks like a picture setting, but it is a verb, as in balancing one thing against another.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a cost is to counterbalance or compensate for it with something equal.

clue.text: One acquiring conviction friend's effort is wasted

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, knocked out of its proper shape

parts.note: the letters of both words, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone trying to win another over finds a friend's work is wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquiring conviction' sounds like becoming persuaded, but it is a court conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A first offender is a person convicted of a crime for the first time in court.

clue.text: Correct and right fare from Turkey

parts.note: done means proper or correct, as in the done thing
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Checking that a Turkish menu is correct and right.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Turkey the country, not the bird. The doner kebab is Turkish street food.
explanation.definitionFit: A doner kebab is Turkish food: spiced meat roasted on a vertical spit and sliced.

clue.text: Passage from "Clemenza di Tito"

indicators.note: taken from a phrase means lifted out of its run of letters

parts.note: the end of Clemenza with di and the start of Tito

explanation.surface: An excerpt from Mozart's opera La Clemenza di Tito.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a piece of music, but it is a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal tunnel into a mine, a passage for access or drainage.

clue.text: Is it a tobogganist's arm?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who rides a small sled
setter's reading: a weapon, a German pistol which shares its name with a sled rider

explanation.surface: A question about what a sledding enthusiast carries.
explanation.walkthrough: The pistol's name is also the word for someone who rides a luge, a small racing toboggan, so the question has a playful yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol, a firearm, which is what arm means here.

clue.text: After forging, had US cent checked

indicators.note: forging is shaping something anew, so the letters are hammered into another form

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: An American coin is examined for counterfeiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' reads as inspected, but it means stopped, as a flow of blood is.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow of blood is to stop it, so staunched means halted or stemmed.

clue.text: Do some shopping — allowed underwear

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, as does to sing
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An errand to buy some underwear is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: Shop is British slang for betraying someone to the police, and so is sing; the surface wants a trip to the stores.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt, a British undergarment.

clue.text: Soldier to spoil works

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to pet a child is to spoil or pamper it

explanation.surface: A soldier sets out to sabotage the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb or a factory, but it is military fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: In military usage, works are defensive fortifications, and a parapet is a protective wall atop them.
